datasets.title: Satellite Detected Waters over Zaporizhzhia Power Plant, Zaporizka Oblast in Ukraine as of 09 June 2023
datasets.description: UNOSAT code FL20230606UKR This map illustrates satellite-detected surface waters using Sentinel-1 images acquired on the 09th of June 2023 at 15:36 UTC. Within the analysed area of 260 km², along the Dnieper River, surface waters appear to have receded by about 12km². The water level of the cooling pond seems to be stable as of 09 June 2023. This is a preliminary analysis and has not yet been validated in the field. Please send ground feedback to the United Nations Satellite Centre (UNOSAT).. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/waters-over-zaporizhzhia-power-plant-zaporizka-oblast-in-ukraine-as-of-09-june-2023]
datasets.details: This is a preliminary assessment and has not yet been validated in the field. It is important to consider the characteristics of the source imagery used in the analyses when interpreting results. For damage assessments it should be noted that only significant damage to the structural integrity of the buildings analyzed can be seen in imagery, while minor damage such as cracks or holes may not be visible at all. For flood extractions using radar data it is important to note that urban areas and highly vegetated areas may mask the flood signature and result in underestimation of flood waters. Users with specific questions or concerns should contact unosat@unitar.org to seek clarification.

lineage.description: UNOSAT analysts processed Sentinel-1 SAR imagery acquired on 09 June 2023 by comparing satellite images to detect notable changes in surface water extent. Water surface area changes were quantified within a 260 km² study area along the Dnieper River, with results delivered as vector geodatabase and shapefile formats for the Zaporizhzhia Power Plant region.

sources.name: UN Operational Satellite Applications Programme (UNOSAT)
sources.description: Sentinel-1 synthetic aperture radar satellite imagery acquired on 09 June 2023 used to detect and map surface water extent changes through multi-temporal image comparison analysis.
